investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-29T01:04–01:05Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurred before any agent was created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway layer, not a confirmed user-facing production outage.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner was rejected with HTTP 502 and error code bad_gateway before any agent lifecycle state could be established. Because all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the same upstream agent-creation step and all returned the identical error message within a ~33-second window, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency rather than to any individual check's logic. No historical pass data exists to establish a regression baseline, so the duration of the outage is unknown from this evidence alone.
